scope.definition: All queue records with first_discovered_at >= explosion_candidate_monitor_state.created_at and city_key present in monitor state.

current_rule_reconstruction.discovery: Telegram and Google News candidates enter the queue only after current city_mentioned() and explosion_relevant() filters. Google publisher_fulltext can rescue discovery but is explicitly review-only.
current_rule_reconstruction.exact_city_check: city_mentioned() over saved title+snippet using current alias list. All 172 live-scope records are mechanically true; spot-check shows this can still have semantic false positives when publisher branding contains the city name.
current_rule_reconstruction.explosion_relevant_check: Current EXPLOSION_TERMS over saved title+snippet. All 172 are mechanically true. The list includes 'ппо', so this is a broad discovery relevance test, not equivalent to strict explosion evidence.
current_rule_reconstruction.explicit_during_alert_check: Literal membership in current three-item EXPLICIT_DURING_TERMS list.
current_rule_reconstruction.immediate_episode_matching: At first discovery only, auto_strict_episode() considers episode/check pairs due in that run with check.label == 'immediate'; publication must be within alert_start .. alert_end+30m, and exactly one episode must match.
current_rule_reconstruction.existing_candidate_behavior: On later rediscovery, add_candidates() updates trigger IDs/check labels/last_seen_at and continues without re-running auto_strict_episode().
current_rule_reconstruction.publisher_fulltext_rule: discovery_basis == publisher_fulltext is never auto-approved by add_candidates(). Current live queue contains zero publisher_fulltext records.
current_rule_reconstruction.metric_propagation: update_explosion_metric_live.py consumes approved_strict/approved_sensitivity records only when matched_episode_id resolves to monitor state; approved strict episode IDs are deduplicated before adding to numerator, then explosions_test.json is copied into dashboard_data.json.explosion_metric_test.

historical_rule_summary: Publication time is not treated as event time. Strict is retained when the source itself explicitly places the explosion during the alert or gives an event time inside the episode.

Require exact-city evidence and event timing inside the sampled alert, or a source that explicitly states the explosion/strike occurred during that alert. Publication time is not event time. Multiple same-day episodes and cross-midnight cases are checked separately. Air-defence-only wording is not strict explosion evidence.
methodology_comparison.comparison: The live auto-approval rule is a deliberately narrower mechanical subset of the historical strict methodology. Historical strict classification accepts exact event time inside the alert or source wording that explicitly binds the event to the alert, and the audited examples also use source event-time language/present-tense context without substituting publication time. The live auto-rule instead requires a small literal EXPLICIT_DURING_TERMS list plus publication inside a unique immediate due window.
methodology_comparison.completeness_consequence: Because needs_review records are not automatically reclassified on later sightings, the live strict metric is incomplete unless the queue is reviewed manually or a controlled reprocessing mechanism is added.
methodology_comparison.formal_spec_limitation: The repo contains usable methodology in historical research artifacts and live-rule descriptions in code/output metadata, but no single centralized formal specification covering the complete strict/sensitivity decision tree for both historical and live processing.

blocker_summary.note: Blocker counts are non-exclusive. A candidate can have multiple mechanical blockers.

near_duplicates_primary_criterion.criterion: start difference <= 90 sec AND end difference <= 90 sec

completed_metric_exposure_diagnostic.caveat: The <=90 sec rule is a diagnostic similarity criterion, not proof that each pair is a true duplicate. Do not repair the denominator from this count alone.

definitions.R0: Current one-shot auto-strict logic reconstructed at first discovery.
definitions.R1: R0 text gates unchanged, but <=90 sec near-duplicate immediate windows count as one logical cluster.
definitions.R2: Current raw immediate windows; remove only the literal explicit_during_alert gate. Publisher-fulltext review-only rule remains.
definitions.R3: R1 logical window dedup plus R2 removal of literal explicit_during_alert gate. Publisher-fulltext review-only rule remains.

replay.caution: R2/R3 are mechanical sensitivity diagnostics. Current explosion_relevant() includes PVO and other broad discovery terms, so R2/R3 eligibility must not be interpreted as a strict-methodology verdict.

classification_throughput.implication: The live metric currently depends heavily on manual queue processing for strict promotions.

queue_latency.code_path_reason: add_candidates() handles an existing candidate by updating trigger_episode_ids/trigger_check_labels/last_seen_at and then continue; auto_strict_episode() is not re-run for existing queue records. No automatic needs_review SLA/reclassification loop was found in the inspected monitor workflow.

limitations: This is a mechanical replay of the current code path, not a content-level strict/sensitivity reclassification of the 98 pending records.
Publication-time matching is reproduced for diagnostics but is not treated as event-time evidence.
Near-duplicate <=90 sec clusters are diagnostic candidates for deduplication, not confirmed duplicate alert episodes.

Current city_mentioned/explosion_relevant checks are discovery filters and can be broader than semantic strict evidence; publisher branding can create a mechanical city hit and 'ппо' can create an explosion-relevance hit.
The artifact does not perform new web/source review; the 12 spot checks use stored queue evidence only.

verdict.main_blocker: NO_EXPLICIT_DURING_ALERT is the most frequent mechanical blocker (95/98), but the immediate-due candidate-to-episode matching design is also material (60/98 have NO_MATCHING_IMMEDIATE_EPISODE).
verdict.kyiv_assessment: Kyiv is the most visible and largest queue backlog (33 pending) and has by far the most near-duplicate clusters (21), but the pending-classification pattern is system-wide across many cities. Kyiv is an outlier in duplicate-window prevalence, not in the existence of the classification backlog.

recommended_fix_sequence_proposal_only: Fix episode identity/matching first: add logical-window dedup or source reconciliation for near duplicates, and decouple candidate matching from 'immediate check happened to be due in the first discovery run'. Preserve ambiguity instead of forcing a match.

Separate discovery relevance from auto-strict evidence before relaxing wording gates. In particular, do not treat the current broad EXPLOSION_TERMS (which includes PVO) as a strict explosion signal; expand air-context vocabulary such as KAB only at the appropriate layer.
After code changes, run a controlled replay of the current queue into a diagnostic artifact without changing statuses; compare R0/new-rule outcomes and inspect a cross-city sample.
Validate on Kyiv plus Dnipro, Mykolaiv, Ternopil, Poltava/Odesa to cover near duplicates, overlapping non-duplicate episodes, late discovery, and literal-wording cases.
Only after validation, reprocess the live queue and update live/canonical metric inputs. Historical baseline/backfill should remain untouched until the live mechanism is proven.
